text: Have you ever forgotten your phone?
style: quiet and intimate, close to the microphone; a man telling you something he has thought about for a long time; understated, almost conversational

text: I don't mean lost it. Just left it somewhere, and carried on as though you hadn't.
style: gentle and unhurried, explaining, with a faint wry warmth
soft, a real question put to the listener, after a small pause

text: You do something often enough, and your brain stops asking you to do it. It just does it for you.
style: thoughtful and matter-of-fact, calm, like someone who has had to understand how this happens

text: Think about the last journey you make every day. What do you actually remember of it?
style: calm and inviting, asking the listener to remember, unhurried
quiet and low, a little rueful

text: I hadn't remembered leaving it. I'd remembered only when I reached for it and it wasn't there.
style: reflective and slower, an unease just beneath the calm

text: The strange thing was, I didn't feel anything missing. The day had gone as it always did. My brain had filled in the rest.
style: quiet and careful, the calm beginning to thin

text: My phone was on the counter.
style: numb, almost to himself, barely holding

text: My phone was on the counter.
style: repeating it, unsteady, the breath catching

text: My phone was on the counter.
style: hollow and very quiet, emptied out
almost no voice left; flat with grief, not performed, very quiet
